item.title: US sending third carrier, 10k more troops to Middle East as Iran tensions persist: Report
item.description: The US is deploying a third aircraft carrier strike group and additional Marine Corps ships to the Middle East. This deployment includes approximately 9,000 to 10,000 troops and comes amid ongoing tensions with Iran. President Donald Trump indicated the possibility of renewed strikes on Iran following the November midterm elections. The US Navy aims to enforce its blockade and ensure security in the region.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: New Jersey homebuyer gets $575K home for $545K, saves $350 a month with incentives
item.description: A New Jersey homebuyer viewed 10 older houses but rejected them after finding costly repairs and maintenance would add to their purchase price. He then considered a new townhouse in Pennsylvania listed at $575,000. After negotiations, he bought it for $545,000 and secured $30,000 in builder incentives, including a mortgage-rate buydown that reduced his rate from 6.25% to 5.25%.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Norway’s melting mountain ice reveals 48 prehistoric arrows, including one up to 6,000 years old
item.description: In a remarkable discovery, Norwegian archaeologists are uncovering ancient treasures as glaciers shrink, revealing 48 prehistoric arrows, including one dated between 5,000 and 6,000 years. This influx of artefacts signifies a shift in our understanding of prehistoric activities as ice melts in the region. The urgency of recovery efforts underscores the impending deterioration of these valuable pieces, highlighting the rapid loss of ice cover around the world.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Illinois ‘caveman’ home built with Colorado rocks is $59,000
item.description: An underground house located in Armington, Illinois, is currently on the market for $59,000. Built in the 1970s, the home features unique rock-lined interiors and circular windows. While the home offers significant size, much of the interior remains unfinished and requires renovation. Buyers should consider potential renovation costs alongside the low asking price per square foot. This property has potential for various uses, including a vacation home or rental.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: How Utah locals pushed Kevin O’Leary to cut his AI data centre plan in half
item.description: Kevin O’Leary-backed plans for a 40,000-acre AI data centre district in Utah have been cut to about 20,000 acres after strong local opposition. Residents have raised concerns over the project’s energy and water use, environmental impact and public review. Developers say the project could create thousands of jobs and support US computing and national defence.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Utah man builds backyard railroad with 40,000 pounds of gravel for $18,000
item.description: Cory Mohl from West Valley City has constructed a remarkable backyard railroad project, aiming to share his love for trains with the community. He dedicated significant time and resources to build around 400 feet of track, attracting local children who delight in riding the miniature train. This charming setup has become a beloved neighborhood fixture, encouraging connections among residents.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Martha Stewart bought Edsel Ford's 63-acre estate in Maine in 1997 and restored its landscape
item.description: In 1997, Martha Stewart took over the Skylands estate, diligently preserving its historic architecture and the stunning landscape, initially crafted by Jens Jensen. This remarkable property, once owned by Edsel Ford, encapsulates pivotal elements of American architectural history connected to the Ford lineage. With the help of landscape architect Patrick Chassé, Stewart revitalized the estate’s gardens to harmonize with the natural environment.

item.title: Pakistan forces kill 7 TTP militants amid rising violence along Afghan border
item.description: Figures from the Centre for Research and Security Studies show that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was Pakistan's worst-hit region for violence in the third quarter of 2025. It recorded 638 violence-related deaths, accounting for nearly 71 per cent of the national total, along with 221 violent incidents, or more than 67 per cent of the total.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: US lawmaker urges Starbucks to close Xinjiang outlet in China over Uyghur oppression
item.description: Moolenaar described Starbucks' decision to operate in Xinjiang as a "morally bankrupt decision", arguing that the company should not be doing business in a region where the US has accused Chinese authorities of widespread abuses against Uyghurs, a mainly Muslim ethnic group. "This is a shocking and morally bankrupt decision by a company that prides itself on social responsibility," he said in a statement published on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Carpenter saved nearly $3 million, funded college for 33 strangers after his death
item.description: An Iowa carpenter who never went to college quietly saved nearly $3 million during his 67-year career. After his death in 2005, the money funded college education for 33 students who could not otherwise afford it. Fourteen years later, the students, known as “Dale’s Kids”, gathered to remember the man they had never met.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indianapolis man quietly built $13 million fortune; after his death, charity got surprise $1.6 million gift
item.description: Terence Kahn, who lived a remarkably simple life, amassed over $13 million before his death in January 2021. After his passing, his estate representatives reached out to various nonprofits in Indianapolis to ensure his wealth was used for good. Among the beneficiaries, Teachers’ Treasures received an impactful donation of $1.6 million, which initiated the nonprofit's inaugural endowment fund and bolstered its mission to distribute essential supplies to teachers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: From red and orange to farmhouse: Couple’s $9,037 kitchen makeover
item.description: Megan and Jeff Hamann embarked on a creative journey to renovate their kitchen in two distinct phases. With a modest budget of under $10,000, they transitioned their once gaudy space into a charming farmhouse-style kitchen. The initial phase prioritized making the kitchen livable, followed by phase two, which included stylish upgrades like new countertops and lighting fixtures, culminating in a space that's both practical and picturesque.

item.title: 4,450 timber pieces restored 110 km of the Murray River, tripling Murray cod numbers
item.description: Researchers restored woody habitat along a 110-km section of Australia's Murray River by adding 4,450 timber structures. Over seven years, Murray cod numbers tripled and golden perch numbers doubled in the restored reach, with fish movement from connected source populations also contributing to the increase.
